meaning: topic marker — 'as for X'. Says what the sentence is about, not who did it.
note: Written は, pronounced wa. Contrast with が, which introduces new or emphasised information.

examples.jp: 私は学生です。
examples.en: I am a student.

meaning: subject marker; also 'but' between clauses.

examples.jp: 猫が好きです。
examples.en: I like cats.

meaning: want to do. Conjugates like an い-adjective.
note: Only for your own desire. Someone else's takes 〜たがる.

examples.jp: 日本へ行きたいです。
examples.en: I want to go to Japan.

meaning: please do. A polite request or instruction.

examples.jp: ちょっと待ってください。
examples.en: Please wait a moment.

meaning: may; it is all right to do.

examples.jp: ここに座ってもいいですか。
examples.en: May I sit here?

formation: Verb ない-form + でください
meaning: please do not do.

examples.jp: 心配しないでください。
examples.en: Please don't worry.

formation: Dictionary form + ことができる
meaning: can; be able to.
note: The potential form (書ける) says the same thing more briefly and is far more common in speech.

examples.jp: 日本語を話すことができます。
examples.en: I can speak Japanese.

formation: Plain form + から / ので
meaning: because. から states your own reason; ので is softer and more objective.

examples.jp: 寒いから、窓を閉めます。
examples.en: It's cold, so I'll close the window.

formation: Dictionary / ない form + ようになる
meaning: come to; reach the point where. A gradual change of state or ability.
note: With a potential verb it means an ability you did not have before.

examples.jp: 日本語が話せるようになりました。
examples.en: I have become able to speak Japanese.

formation: Dictionary / ない form + ようにする
meaning: make an effort to; see to it that. A habit you are trying to keep.

examples.jp: 毎日運動するようにしています。
examples.en: I make a point of exercising every day.

formation: Dictionary / ない form + ことにする
meaning: decide to. The decision is yours.
note: Compare 〜ことになる, where the decision is made for you.

examples.jp: 留学することにしました。
examples.en: I've decided to study abroad.

formation: Dictionary / ない form + ことになる
meaning: it has been decided that; it turns out that. Decided by circumstance or by someone else.

examples.jp: 来月、東京に行くことになりました。
examples.en: It's been decided that I'll go to Tokyo next month.

meaning: I hear that; they say that. Reporting what you were told.
note: Distinguished from the 'looks like' そうだ by what comes before it: plain form here, verb stem or adjective stem there.

examples.jp: 明日は雨が降るそうです。
examples.en: I hear it's going to rain tomorrow.

formation: Plain form + ようだ; Noun + のようだ
meaning: it seems; it looks as though. Based on what you can see or sense.
note: みたいだ is the casual equivalent.

examples.jp: 誰かいるようです。
examples.en: It seems someone is here.

meaning: apparently; seems (from what you have heard). Also 'typical of' after a noun.

examples.jp: 彼は来ないらしい。
examples.en: Apparently he isn't coming.

meaning: ought to be; is supposed to be. A confident expectation with a reason behind it.
note: 〜はずがない is the strong denial: 'there's no way that'.

examples.jp: 彼はもう着いているはずです。
examples.en: He should have arrived by now.

meaning: while doing. Two things at once by the same person.
note: The main action is the second clause; the ながら clause is the background one.

examples.jp: 音楽を聞きながら勉強します。
examples.en: I study while listening to music.

formation: Noun + において; Noun + における + Noun
meaning: in; at; on. The formal written replacement for で, used for places, fields and occasions.
note: Belongs to written and formal Japanese. Saying it in casual conversation sounds like reading from a report.

examples.jp: 会議は東京において行われた。
examples.en: The meeting was held in Tokyo.

formation: Noun + に対して; Noun + に対する + Noun
meaning: towards; with regard to; in contrast with. Marks the target of an attitude or action.
note: Also used to set two things against each other: 'whereas'.

examples.jp: 先生に対して失礼なことを言った。
examples.en: He said something rude to the teacher.

meaning: about; concerning. The topic of talking, thinking or writing.

examples.jp: この問題について話しましょう。
examples.en: Let's talk about this problem.

meaning: by means of; due to; depending on. Also marks the agent in a passive sentence.
note: Four distinct uses — cause, means, agent, and 'varies with' — separated only by context.

examples.jp: 人によって考え方が違う。
examples.en: Ways of thinking differ from person to person.

meaning: for; from the standpoint of. Whose judgement this is.
note: Takes an evaluation, not an action: 〜にとって大切だ, not 〜にとって行く.

examples.jp: 私にとって家族が一番大切です。
examples.en: For me, family is the most important thing.

formation: Noun + に関して; Noun + に関する + Noun
meaning: regarding; concerning. The formal counterpart of について.

examples.jp: その件に関しては後で話します。
examples.en: I'll speak about that matter later.

formation: Noun + を通じて / を通して
meaning: through; by way of; throughout (a period).

examples.jp: 友人を通じて彼を知った。
examples.en: I got to know him through a friend.

meaning: on the basis of; using as material.

examples.jp: 実話をもとに映画が作られた。
examples.en: The film was made based on a true story.

meaning: based on; in accordance with. Stricter than をもとに — a rule or principle being followed.

examples.jp: 法律に基づいて処理する。
examples.en: It will be handled in accordance with the law.

formation: Noun + から + Noun + にかけて
meaning: from … through …. A vague span of time or space.
note: Unlike 〜から〜まで, the endpoints are approximate.

examples.jp: 夜から朝にかけて雪が降った。
examples.en: It snowed from night through to morning.

meaning: over; spanning; throughout. Emphasises how large the span is.

examples.jp: 工事は三年にわたって続いた。
examples.en: The construction went on for three years.

formation: Plain form / Noun + の + おかげで
meaning: thanks to. A cause with a welcome result.
note: Paired with 〜せいで, which is the same structure for an unwelcome result.

examples.jp: 先生のおかげで合格できました。
examples.en: Thanks to my teacher, I was able to pass.

formation: Plain form / Noun + の + せいで
meaning: because of (blame). せいか softens it to 'perhaps because'.

examples.jp: 雨のせいで試合が中止になった。
examples.en: The match was cancelled because of the rain.

formation: Plain form / Noun + の + ために
meaning: because of; for the purpose of. Objective cause, or a goal.
note: With a volitional verb it is purpose; with a state or past event it is cause.

examples.jp: 事故のために電車が遅れた。
examples.en: The train was late because of an accident.

meaning: now that; since. A fact that obliges a conclusion.
note: The second clause usually carries duty, determination or advice.

examples.jp: 約束した以上、守らなければならない。
examples.en: Now that I've promised, I have to keep it.

meaning: now that; as long as. Like 以上は, with more personal resolve.

examples.jp: やるからには最後までやる。
examples.en: If I'm going to do it, I'll see it through.

meaning: from the fact that; which is why. Gives the evidence for a name or conclusion.

examples.jp: 形が富士山に似ていることから、こう呼ばれる。
examples.en: It is called this because its shape resembles Mt Fuji.

formation: Plain form / Noun + にもかかわらず
meaning: despite; in spite of. Formal, and stronger than のに.

examples.jp: 雨にもかかわらず試合は行われた。
examples.en: The match went ahead despite the rain.

formation: Verb stem / い-adj / Noun + ながら(も)
meaning: although; even though. Not the 'while doing' ながら.
note: Told apart from simultaneous-action ながら by the clash in meaning between the two clauses.

examples.jp: 残念ながら、参加できません。
examples.en: Regrettably, I can't take part.

formation: Plain form / Noun + の + くせに
meaning: even though; and yet. Carries criticism or contempt.
note: Never neutral. Using it about yourself, or to a superior, is a mistake.

examples.jp: 知っているくせに教えてくれない。
examples.en: He knows but won't tell me.

meaning: although; but. Written, and concedes a fact before undercutting it.

examples.jp: 買ったものの、一度も使っていない。
examples.en: I bought it, but I've never once used it.

formation: Plain form / Noun + どころか
meaning: far from; let alone. Denies what was expected and replaces it with the opposite.

examples.jp: 漢字どころかひらがなも読めない。
examples.en: Far from kanji, he can't even read hiragana.

formation: Plain form / Noun + の + わりに
meaning: considering; for a …. Something does not match what you would expect from it.

examples.jp: 値段のわりにおいしい。
examples.en: It's tasty for the price.

meaning: to the extent that; about. Measures how much by comparing.
note: In 〜ば〜ほど it means 'the more … the more'.

examples.jp: 泣きたいほど嬉しかった。
examples.en: I was so happy I could have cried.

formation: Verb ば-form + dictionary form + ほど
meaning: the more …, the more ….

examples.jp: 考えれば考えるほど分からなくなる。
examples.en: The more I think, the less I understand.

meaning: about; to the point of. Often marks something as trivially small.

examples.jp: 自分の部屋くらい掃除しなさい。
examples.en: At least clean your own room.

formation: Noun + ばかり; Verb て-form + ばかりいる
meaning: nothing but; only. Complains that it is always the same thing.
note: Verb た + ばかり is different again: 'just did'.

examples.jp: 彼はゲームばかりしている。
examples.en: He does nothing but play games.

formation: Plain form / Noun + ばかりでなく
meaning: not only … but also.

examples.jp: 彼は英語ばかりでなく中国語も話せる。
examples.en: He speaks not only English but Chinese too.

formation: Plain form / Noun + だけでなく
meaning: not only … but also. The everyday version of ばかりでなく.

examples.jp: 味だけでなく見た目もいい。
examples.en: Not only the taste but the look of it is good.

meaning: on top of that; in addition. Both clauses must lean the same way.

examples.jp: 安い上においしい。
examples.en: It's cheap, and on top of that it's delicious.

formation: Plain form / Noun + というより
meaning: rather than; more … than. Corrects a description.

examples.jp: 寒いというより痛い。
examples.en: It's painful rather than cold.

meaning: must be; no doubt. A confident inference.

examples.jp: 彼は知っているに違いない。
examples.en: He must know.

meaning: there's no way that; it's impossible that.

examples.jp: そんなことがあるわけがない。
examples.en: There's no way that could happen.

formation: Plain form + わけではない
meaning: it doesn't mean that; not necessarily. A partial denial.
note: Denies an inference someone might draw, not the fact itself.

examples.jp: 嫌いなわけではない。
examples.en: It's not that I dislike it.

meaning: that's why; no wonder. The conclusion that follows naturally.

examples.jp: 道理で寒いわけだ。
examples.en: No wonder it's cold.

meaning: cannot possibly be. Denies on the strength of a reason.

examples.jp: 彼が犯人のはずがない。
examples.en: There's no way he's the culprit.

formation: Plain form + かもしれない
meaning: might; may. Low confidence.

examples.jp: 明日は雨が降るかもしれない。
examples.en: It might rain tomorrow.

formation: Dictionary / ている / た + ところだ
meaning: about to / in the middle of / just finished. Which one depends on the form before it.

examples.jp: 今から出かけるところです。
examples.en: I'm just about to go out.

meaning: just did. How recent it feels, not how recent it was.
note: Differs from 〜たところ, which is objectively a moment ago.

examples.jp: 日本に来たばかりです。
examples.en: I've only just come to Japan.

meaning: keep doing; go on doing.

examples.jp: 三時間歩き続けた。
examples.en: I kept walking for three hours.

formation: Verb stem + 始める / 出す
meaning: start doing. 〜出す adds suddenness.

examples.jp: 急に泣き出した。
examples.en: She suddenly burst into tears.

meaning: finish doing.

examples.jp: 本を読み終わった。
examples.en: I finished reading the book.

meaning: do completely; do by accident (and regret it).
note: Contracts to 〜ちゃう / 〜じゃう in speech.

examples.jp: 財布を忘れてしまった。
examples.en: I've gone and forgotten my wallet.

meaning: do in advance; leave something done.

examples.jp: 先に予約しておきます。
examples.en: I'll book it in advance.

meaning: has been done (and remains so). Someone did it on purpose.
note: 〜ている with an intransitive verb describes the same scene without an agent.

examples.jp: 窓が開けてある。
examples.en: The window has been left open.

formation: Verb て-form + いく / くる
meaning: go on doing (from now) / have been doing (up to now). Direction in time or space.

examples.jp: だんだん寒くなってきた。
examples.en: It's been getting colder.

formation: て-form of adjective or verb + たまらない
meaning: unbearably; can't stand how ….

examples.jp: 暑くてたまらない。
examples.en: It's unbearably hot.

formation: て-form + しかたがない / しょうがない
meaning: can't help feeling; terribly.

examples.jp: 心配でしかたがない。
examples.en: I can't stop worrying.

meaning: tends to; prone to. Almost always something unwanted.

examples.jp: 最近、休みがちだ。
examples.en: He's been absent a lot lately.

meaning: a touch of; slightly. A hint of a condition.

examples.jp: 風邪気味です。
examples.en: I have a bit of a cold.

meaning: -ish; looks like; tends to.

examples.jp: 子供っぽい。
examples.en: He's childish.

meaning: half-done; in the middle of.

examples.jp: 読みかけの本。
examples.en: A book I'm part-way through.

meaning: might well (something bad); is capable of.
note: Only ever for undesirable outcomes.

examples.jp: 事故になりかねない。
examples.en: It could well lead to an accident.

formation: Verb ない-stem + ざるを得ない
meaning: have no choice but to. Formal.
note: する becomes せざるを得ない, not しざる.

examples.jp: 認めざるを得ない。
examples.en: I have no choice but to admit it.

formation: Dictionary form + よりほかない / しかない
meaning: there's nothing for it but to.

examples.jp: 待つしかない。
examples.en: There's nothing to do but wait.

meaning: should; ought to. A moral judgement, not a rule.
note: する takes both するべき and すべき.

examples.jp: もっと早く言うべきだった。
examples.en: You should have said so sooner.

formation: Verb ない-stem + ければならない
meaning: must; have to. An external obligation.

examples.jp: 明日までに出さなければならない。
examples.en: I have to hand it in by tomorrow.

formation: Verb ない-stem + くてもいい
meaning: don't have to.

examples.jp: 無理に来なくてもいいですよ。
examples.en: You don't have to force yourself to come.

meaning: if; when. たら is general, ば is hypothetical, なら responds to what was just said, と is automatic consequence.
note: The one N3 point most worth drilling as a set rather than one at a time — they overlap, and choosing wrongly is the commonest intermediate mistake.

examples.jp: 春になると桜が咲く。
examples.en: When spring comes, the cherries bloom.

meaning: should have; I wish I had.

examples.jp: もっと勉強すればよかった。
examples.en: I should have studied more.

formation: Verb た-form + らどうですか
meaning: why don't you …? A suggestion.

examples.jp: 少し休んだらどうですか。
examples.en: Why don't you take a rest?

formation: Verb た-form / ない-form + ほうがいい
meaning: had better; it's better to.
note: The past form is the advice form: 行ったほうがいい, not 行くほうがいい.

examples.jp: 早く寝たほうがいい。
examples.en: You'd better go to bed early.

meaning: I think I'll; I intend to.

examples.jp: 来年、留学しようと思っています。
examples.en: I'm thinking of studying abroad next year.

formation: Dictionary / ない form + つもりだ
meaning: intend to; plan to. A settled intention.

examples.jp: 今年は車を買うつもりです。
examples.en: I plan to buy a car this year.

meaning: try to; be about to.

examples.jp: 出かけようとしたとき、電話が鳴った。
examples.en: Just as I was about to leave, the phone rang.

meaning: there's no need to.

examples.jp: 心配することはない。
examples.en: There's no need to worry.

meaning: it is the way things are; used to. A general truth, or nostalgia.

examples.jp: 時間が経つのは早いものだ。
examples.en: Time really does fly.

formation: Plain form + ということだ
meaning: it is said that; it means that.

examples.jp: 彼は来ないということだ。
examples.en: Apparently he isn't coming.

meaning: called; named. Introduces something the listener does not know.

examples.jp: 田中という人から電話がありました。
examples.en: There was a call from someone called Tanaka.

meaning: according to. Names the source, and pairs with そうだ at the end.

examples.jp: 天気予報によると、明日は晴れるそうだ。
examples.en: According to the forecast, it'll be fine tomorrow.

meaning: even. Picks an extreme case to make the point.
note: 〜さえ〜ば means 'if only'.

examples.jp: 子供でさえ知っている。
examples.en: Even a child knows that.

meaning: if only; as long as. One condition is enough.

examples.jp: お金さえあれば買える。
examples.en: As long as I have the money, I can buy it.

meaning: precisely; it is exactly this that.

examples.jp: 今年こそ合格したい。
examples.en: This year for sure I want to pass.

meaning: only; nothing but. Always with a negative verb, and faintly regretful.
note: だけ is neutral; しか implies it is not enough.

examples.jp: 千円しかない。
examples.en: I've only got a thousand yen.

formation: Dictionary form / Noun + の + たびに
meaning: every time; whenever.

examples.jp: 会うたびに背が伸びている。
examples.en: Every time I see him he's taller.

formation: Dictionary / ない / ている form + うちに
meaning: while; before it changes. Do it before the chance is gone.
note: 〜ないうちに is 'before it happens'.

examples.jp: 暗くならないうちに帰ろう。
examples.en: Let's go home before it gets dark.

formation: Plain form / Noun + の + 間に
meaning: while; during. 間 alone is the whole stretch; 間に is a moment inside it.

examples.jp: 留守の間に手紙が届いた。
examples.en: A letter arrived while I was out.

formation: Dictionary / た form / Noun + の + とおりに
meaning: just as; in the way that.

examples.jp: 説明書のとおりに組み立てた。
examples.en: I assembled it just as the instructions said.

formation: た-form / ない-form / Noun + の + まま
meaning: as it is; leaving it unchanged. Often with a hint that it should have changed.

examples.jp: 靴を履いたまま入らないでください。
examples.en: Please don't come in with your shoes on.

formation: た-form + きり; Noun + きり
meaning: only; and that was the last of it.

examples.jp: 彼とは一度会ったきりだ。
examples.en: I met him once and that was it.

meaning: want someone (else) to do.
note: The person asked is marked with に.

examples.jp: もう少し待ってほしい。
examples.en: I'd like you to wait a bit longer.

meaning: shows signs of wanting to. Used of a third person.
note: You cannot see inside someone else, so their desire is described as behaviour.

examples.jp: 子供が外へ行きたがっている。
examples.en: The child wants to go outside.

meaning: passive. Also the 'suffering passive', where something is done to your detriment.

examples.jp: 雨に降られた。
examples.en: I got caught in the rain.

meaning: causative: make or let someone do.
note: を for 'make', に for 'let', when the verb is intransitive.

examples.jp: 子供に野菜を食べさせた。
examples.en: I made the child eat vegetables.

meaning: be made to do. Always unwilling.

examples.jp: 二時間も待たされた。
examples.en: I was kept waiting two whole hours.

formation: お + Verb stem + になる
meaning: honorific: raises the person you are talking about.

examples.jp: 先生はもうお帰りになりました。
examples.en: The teacher has already gone home.

meaning: humble: lowers yourself to raise the listener.

examples.jp: お荷物をお持ちします。
examples.en: Let me carry your bag.

meaning: whether or not.

examples.jp: 行くかどうかまだ決めていない。
examples.en: I haven't decided whether to go.

meaning: for the purpose of; used for. Not the concessive のに.

examples.jp: この道具は野菜を切るのに使う。
examples.en: This tool is used for cutting vegetables.

meaning: in order to. The subject must be the same in both clauses.

examples.jp: 健康のために毎日歩く。
examples.en: I walk every day for my health.

formation: Potential / ない form + ように
meaning: so that. Used when the outcome is not directly under your control.
note: ために takes a volitional verb, ように a non-volitional one — the distinction N3 actually tests.

examples.jp: 忘れないようにメモした。
examples.en: I made a note so I wouldn't forget.

formation: Verb stem + にくい / やすい
meaning: hard to / easy to do.

examples.jp: この字は読みにくい。
examples.en: This handwriting is hard to read.

formation: Verb stem / adjective stem + すぎる
meaning: too much; excessively.

examples.jp: 食べすぎて動けない。
examples.en: I ate too much and can't move.

meaning: the way of doing; how to.

examples.jp: 漢字の書き方を教えてください。
examples.en: Please teach me how to write kanji.

formation: Noun + みたいに / のように
meaning: like; in the manner of.

examples.jp: 子供のように喜んだ。
examples.en: He was as delighted as a child.

meaning: as; in the capacity of.

examples.jp: 彼は医者として働いている。
examples.en: He works as a doctor.

formation: Plain form / Noun + の + かわりに
meaning: instead of; in exchange for.

examples.jp: 父のかわりに私が行きます。
examples.en: I'll go instead of my father.

meaning: on the other hand; while. Two true sides of one thing.

examples.jp: 便利な反面、値段が高い。
examples.en: It's convenient, but on the other hand expensive.

meaning: while; meanwhile. Sets two facts side by side.

examples.jp: 収入が増える一方で、支出も増えた。
examples.en: While income rose, so did spending.

meaning: on behalf of; in place of.

examples.jp: 社長に代わって挨拶します。
examples.en: I'll give the address on behalf of the president.

meaning: compared with.

examples.jp: 去年に比べて寒い。
examples.en: It's cold compared with last year.

formation: Dictionary form / Noun + にしたがって
meaning: as … proceeds, … . Two things changing together.

examples.jp: 年を取るにつれて記憶力が落ちる。
examples.en: As you age, your memory declines.

meaning: the moment that; no sooner than. The second event is a surprise.
note: Cannot be used for something you planned — it must be unexpected.

examples.jp: ドアを開けたとたん、猫が逃げた。
examples.en: The moment I opened the door, the cat ran off.

formation: ている / た form + ところに
meaning: just as; right at the moment when.

examples.jp: 出かけるところに電話が来た。
examples.en: Just as I was leaving, a call came.

meaning: other than; apart from.

examples.jp: 私以外は全員来た。
examples.en: Everyone but me came.

meaning: without; leaving out.

examples.jp: 冗談抜きで話そう。
examples.en: Let's talk seriously, joking aside.

formation: Dictionary / ない form + 限り
meaning: as far as; as long as.

examples.jp: 私の知る限り、彼は正直だ。
examples.en: As far as I know, he's honest.

formation: Dictionary form / Noun + に際して
meaning: on the occasion of. Formal, for significant moments.

examples.jp: 開会に際して一言申し上げます。
examples.en: Let me say a word on the occasion of this opening.

formation: Dictionary form / Noun + にあたって
meaning: on the occasion of; prior to. Formal, before something important.

examples.jp: 出発にあたって注意事項を確認する。
examples.en: Before departure, we'll go over the precautions.

meaning: what was it again? Casual, asking yourself or a friend to confirm.

examples.jp: 明日、何時だっけ。
examples.en: What time was it tomorrow again?

meaning: as if; there's no way I would. An emphatic refusal.

examples.jp: 二度と行くものか。
examples.en: I'm never going there again.

meaning: even if; no matter how much. The effort will not help.

examples.jp: 急いだところで間に合わない。
examples.en: Even if I hurry, I won't make it.

formation: Plain form / Noun + にすぎない
meaning: is no more than; merely.

examples.jp: それは言い訳にすぎない。
examples.en: That's nothing but an excuse.

meaning: unlike; in contrast to.

examples.jp: 兄と違って、私は運動が苦手だ。
examples.en: Unlike my brother, I'm bad at sport.

formation: Verb て-form + ばかりはいられない
meaning: can't just keep doing; can't afford to.

examples.jp: 泣いてばかりはいられない。
examples.en: I can't just keep crying.

meaning: precisely because; all the more so because.

examples.jp: 期待していただけに残念だ。
examples.en: It's disappointing precisely because I had hopes.

meaning: as much as; to the extent one can.

examples.jp: できるだけ早く来てください。
examples.en: Please come as soon as you can.

meaning: even doing; not even.

examples.jp: 名前さえ書けなかった。
examples.en: He couldn't even write his name.

meaning: have a feeling that.

examples.jp: どこかで会った気がする。
examples.en: I feel like we've met somewhere.

formation: Verb た-form + ことがある
meaning: have done before; there are times when.

examples.jp: 富士山に登ったことがある。
examples.en: I've climbed Mt Fuji before.

formation: Dictionary / ない form + ように言う
meaning: tell someone to. Reports an instruction.

examples.jp: 静かにするように言われた。
examples.en: I was told to be quiet.

meaning: should; it would be good if. Also 'all you have to do is'.

examples.jp: 分からなければ聞けばいい。
examples.en: If you don't understand, just ask.

meaning: aimed at (向け) / suited to (向き).
note: 向け is a deliberate target; 向き is a natural fit.

examples.jp: 子供向けの本。
examples.en: A book aimed at children.

meaning: covered in; full of. Always something unpleasant.

examples.jp: 間違いだらけの作文。
examples.en: An essay riddled with mistakes.

formation: Verb stem / adjective stem + そうだ
meaning: looks like; seems about to. From what you can see.
note: いい becomes よさそう and ない becomes なさそう — both irregular and both tested.

examples.jp: 雨が降りそうだ。
examples.en: It looks like it's going to rain.

meaning: after doing. Emphasises the order.

examples.jp: 手を洗ってから食べなさい。
examples.en: Wash your hands before you eat.

formation: Verb た-form / Noun + の + あとで
meaning: after.

examples.jp: 食事のあとで散歩した。
examples.en: I took a walk after the meal.

formation: Dictionary form / Noun + の + 前に
meaning: before.
note: Always the dictionary form, never the past, however long ago it was.

examples.jp: 寝る前に歯を磨く。
examples.en: I brush my teeth before bed.
